doc.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The household piano and Uncle Buster's house-rent parties
summary: Unlike neighbors, his family really played the piano; uncle Robert 'Buster' York played badly at rent parties with food and records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay. We’ve progressed a bit. When you were taking piano lessons, there was a piano in the house.

There was always a piano in the house. It seems like everybody in the neighborhood had a piano. But nobody played them. They put pictures on it, doilies, and all kind of things on the piano, but it was never played.
So it was a piece of furniture.

Piece of furniture. But our house was different. I had two uncles that played. My uncle’s name was Robert – Robert York – but everybody used to call him Buster. Sometimes they’d have these house-rent parties, where they serve food and drink and stuff, and make the money – generate money to pay the rent. They used to hire people to play sometimes. They used to hire him to play. I can’t understand why. He played terrible. Piano music by Buster. He had a reputation. Wherever you saw Buster’s name on the flyer, you said, “Oh. This is going to be great.” They would serve pig feet and chitlins, potato salad, cole slaw, and beer. Be playing the records with the lights down dim. It was fantastic. I remember those days.
